name: @fossil-lang/playground
description: The loop, clickable: write a .fossil program in a browser tab, type-check it as you type, run it, get a corpus, query the corpus — all client-side, no server, the source bytes never leaving the machine. Never published; the pnpm-workspace entry is for resolution, not for npm.
//scripts: `build` type-checks first, because a playground that compiles but cannot resolve @fossil-lang/wasm's pkg/ is a build that passes and an app that white-screens. The three workspace dependencies each need their own `build` run first (each shells out to cargo + wasm-bindgen); `pnpm --filter @fossil-lang/playground... build` in the workflow is what orders that.
//bench: `bench` writes the large demo corpus into public/bench/ (gitignored, ~56 MB, ~5 s) by calling apps/corpus/guards/fixture.mjs — the SAME generator the corpus guards use, not a copy. It is deliberately NOT part of `dev` or `build`: it needs the `duckdb` binary on PATH, and a playground that refuses to start because an optional demo asset is missing would be the worse app. The streaming panel says how to generate it when it is absent. `verify-stream` checks the tile arithmetic against real bytes over a real HTTP server with Range, and needs `bench` to have run. `verify-canvas` drives the SAME `BoundedSource` the canvas mounts, over the same corpus, through the `duckdb` binary instead of a GPU — it is the automatable half of that panel, because cosmos.gl draws from `requestAnimationFrame` and a browser fires none in a tab that is not visible, which a tab opened under automation is not. `verify-properties` is the three properties a level-of-detail view owes its reader -- fidelity against a null, monotone refinement, path independence -- through the door rather than through this app's own SQL, and `verify-nesting` asserts the one property of the sample that a count cannot see: that zooming in REFINES the picture rather than replacing it, by importing `src/stride.ts`'s expression and checking that each zoom's drawn set contains the previous one's, restricted to what is still in frame.
//kanzo-tech: The version is exact, not a range: 0.1.0 is the first non-prerelease, and one exact pin is what a consumer of a young library owes it. It also drops the @duckdb/duckdb-wasm peer, so the inert 1.32.0-vs-1.33.1-dev57.0 warning `pnpm install` used to print is gone. What the bump did NOT fix is the tooltip surface: `CodeEditor`'s theme reads `var(--popover)` with no fallback and only kanzo's DARK palettes define that token — see the `--popover` block in src/styles.css, which is where every CodeMirror tooltip in this app got its background back. The @codemirror/* set is here rather than there because they are all OPTIONAL peers of @kanzo-tech/ui — its CodeEditor externalises every one and resolves them from the consumer.
//kanzo-graph: @kanzo-tech/graph is the renderer, and the duckdb pin that used to keep it out is GONE from ITS manifest: 0.1.0 names @duckdb/duckdb-wasm nowhere, because the Mosaic half moved to @kanzo-tech/mosaic and the coordinator stopped arriving through @kanzo-tech/ui/analytics. It did not vanish from the world — @uwdata/mosaic-core@0.29.2 holds 1.33.1-dev57.0 as a HARD dependency — so adopting @kanzo-tech/mosaic would put a second engine, and therefore a second crossfilter, in this bundle. It is an OPTIONAL peer living entirely on the ./duckdb subpath and this app does not import it: src/tiles.ts implements BoundedSource directly over the app's own connection, so no coordinator is created and no crossfilter exists to join. Measured, not assumed: the built bundle carries one duckdb wasm asset. What reverses this is a chart beside the canvas AND the two pins agreeing.
